source_text: Secundum haec, inquit, faciebant prophetis patres eorum. o Christum uersipellem, nunc destructorem nunc adsertorem prophetarum! destruebat ut aemulus, conuertens discipulos eorum sibi, adserebat ut amicus, suggillans insectatores eorum.
pass_a_gloss: According to these things, he says, the fathers of the prophets were doing. Oh Christ, changeling, now destroyer, now defender of the prophets! He was destroying as a rival, turning their disciples to himself, he was defending as a friend, reproving those who harassed them.

choices.why: accurate translation of the Latin word

pass_b_english: "That's how their fathers treated the prophets," he says. "Oh, you shapeshifter Christ -- now the prophets' destroyer, now their defender! You tore them down as a rival, stealing their disciples for yourself; you propped them up as a friend, shaming the ones who harassed them."

anf_compare.notes: Drafted from source only; ANF not shown to drafter.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A correctly translates 'uersipellem' as 'changeling' and 'suggillans' as 'reproving'. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that maintains the meaning of the original clauses, including the distinction between the roles of destroyer and defender.
